variants.mechanism: Tail fixed; two-leaf wings retain proposed backward folding. Equipment pads on central tail, not motor caps.
variants.direction:
L65 — FIXED CENTERLINE TAIL, developed from L63.
Input 3 is real or_elite: borrow only its stepped, raked longitudinal aft profile and solid mounting-face vocabulary. Do not copy its cockpit, third engine, wing system or its actual equipment-to-engine ownership. Input 4 is the real LI cargo-door sweep, used only to keep this tail behind it.
Build one broad-rooted but transversely NARROW aft keel on the central stern. In SIDE, a strong diagonal leading face rises behind the hatch, followed by TWO deliberate offset ledges toward the rear: a medium lower shoulder for paired side mounting pads and a smaller upper shoulder with one inclined pad. Shape the top as a short clipped aft-swept cap, not a simple tall triangle and not a horizontal crossbar. In FRONT it is one compact central blade, substantially narrower than the distance between engine centers; no parts above either engine. Width at its root is sufficient for a credible rigid attachment. Height above roof roughly comparable to hull body depth, considerably smaller than a giant sail. Preserve a little native fan relief below the functional mounting faces.
The tail is FIXED and identical in SIDE FLIGHT and SIDE STOWED. Only the existing two-leaf wing assemblies fold. Keep L63 body/engines/collar/roof/wing contours otherwise unchanged. Label L65.
variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / functional tail redesign.
Create ONE revised li_pir_elite concept sheet from the positively reviewed base artwork. The owner likes its basic body, collar, horizontally separated engines and foldable two-leaf wings. NOW REMOVE THE ENTIRE TRANSVERSE SPOILER/CROSSBAR ABOVE THE TWO ENGINES and replace it with a purpose-designed CENTERLINE TAIL for EQUIPMENT MOUNTS. This is not another styling change to the old crossbar.

INPUT 1 is the BASE SHIP TO PRESERVE, except its crossbar and rear equipment placement.
INPUT 2 is the immutable real native LI cockpit and collar. It overrides projection inaccuracies in the AI base: same cabin shell, glass boundaries, pane frames, proportions and the original three sharp collar ribs. Keep collar fully visible; no brow, hood or enlarged canopy.
Other input roles are specified with the variant below.

PRESERVE:
The base's integrated broad rear engine shoulders, TWO horizontally separated aft-facing polygonal nozzles, central body proportions, CLOSED FLAT ROOF with flush baydoor seams, native red-brown/ochre panels and restrained Liberty fan artwork. Preserve the two distinct folding wing leaves on EACH side, their front-side roots and backward/inward nesting below the engine shoulders. No third engine or return to a vertical stack. No new center roof trench, obelisks, long side walls, aircraft bubble cockpit, exposed pipes or skeleton.

TAIL / EQUIPMENT PURPOSE:
Completely remove the long left-to-right cap connecting the engine shoulders. Both motor tops become individual plain service housings, without yellow equipment pads or mounting sockets on their upper caps. Remove former rear equipment sockets from these motor-top surfaces; keep unrelated native cockpit and wing mounts.
The NEW tail is a solid, compact, longitudinal centerline structure, attached to the central rear bulkhead BETWEEN the left and right engine housings and BEHIND the cargo-door footprint. It is not supported by a transverse beam over the engines. Its main equipment mounting faces are above the CENTRAL fuselage line, laterally inboard of both nozzles, not directly above either engine.
Design deliberate locally thick FLAT mounting faces with visible native small metallic hardpoint plates: two opposed lateral/rearward flats on the tail, plus one small upper inclined pad with useful clearance. These three illustrative pads move to a clear location on the tail. Show them without installed guns, missiles, antennas or bulky modules. They are concept mounting areas, not a new approved loadout or an engineering validation. Avoid covering the mounting face with ornament; a plain functional pad matters more than a decorative fin.
Leave readable physical separation between the pads, cargo door sweep, side wings and engine service housings. No equipment directly behind a nozzle. The new tail can rise modestly, following Order / LI elite2, but must remain proportionate and not become a cathedral mast. Functional integrated geometry, few strong angular planes; controlled native relief only.

CARGO CONSTRAINT:
Native LI pirate has two long upper doors opening outward/upward. Keep the new tail base and all motion aft of those doors. DO NOT copy LI elite2's long forward tail foot, since that source has no active equivalent baydoor animation. Show the central hatch CLOSED and FLUSH, with no sunken channel. Do not use the new tail as a decorative lid over the cargo hatch.

MATERIAL:
The same maintained pirate Liberty finish, only restrained wear and a few subtle replacement panels. No wreck damage, major rust, chains, skulls, flags, gothic decoration or shiny gilding. Preserve the dominant ribbed collar and original body: the new tail supports useful equipment placement.

SHEET:
Light grey background. Large long-lens front-side three-quarter, nose LEFT, showing original collar, new tail side and ordinary-size cabin. Medium REAR THREE-QUARTER clearly shows two lateral engines, NO transverse crossbar, and new central tail/mount locations. Smaller FRONT, SIDE FLIGHT, TOP, SIDE STOWED. Same geometry across views. The SIDE pair must use matching scale/camera so tail movement (or the absence of tail motion in the fixed variant) is credible. Wing leaves in STOWED overlap without shrinking. Clear labels only ID and view names.

Build one broad-rooted but transversely NARROW aft keel on the central stern. In SIDE, a strong diagonal leading face rises behind the hatch, followed by TWO deliberate offset ledges toward the rear: a medium lower shoulder for paired side mounting pads and a smaller upper shoulder with one inclined pad. Shape the top as a short clipped aft-swept cap, not a simple tall triangle and not a horizontal crossbar. In FRONT it is one compact central blade, substantially narrower than the distance between engine centers; no parts above either engine. Width at its root is sufficient for a credible rigid attachment. Height above roof roughly comparable to hull body depth, considerably smaller than a giant sail. Preserve a little native fan relief below the functional mounting faces.
The tail is FIXED and identical in SIDE FLIGHT and SIDE STOWED. Only the existing two-leaf wing assemblies fold. Keep L63 body/engines/collar/roof/wing contours otherwise unchanged. Label L65.

observations: L63 engine shoulders, twin lateral nozzles, two-leaf wings and exposed native-style collar remain recognizable.
Transverse spoiler across the engine housings is removed; motor tops are individually closed and free of former equipment sockets.
Central stepped aft tail carries visibly distinct mounting faces and a small upper pad. These are proposed mounting surfaces, not assigned equipment or HPs.
Matched SIDE states keep the fixed tail essentially unchanged while illustrating wing folding.
Closed roof remains; the tail begins near the rear hatch end, but actual baydoor sweep clearance is not validated.
Exact mounting-face count/orientation and cabin contours vary across the perspectives; the original cabin and actual mounting geometry must govern modeling.

variants.mechanism: Proposed fixed central tail root plus two nested moving leaves using combined small rotations/slides inspired by LI elite2; exact new clearance unvalidated.
variants.direction:
L66 — FOLDING COMPOUND CENTERLINE TAIL, developed from L64.
Input 3 is real li_elite2: reference for a layered moving tail carrying equipment. Input 4 shows its actual motion: two sections translate a SHORT distance and rotate a SMALL amount to overlap. It does NOT collapse flat to the deck. Do not invent a 90-degree fold. Input 5 is the native LI cargo-door sweep that must stay clear; do not copy li_elite2's long tail foot over that region.
Replace L64's crossbar with a short fixed solid central stern root and TWO distinct overlapping polygonal tail leaves above it. In SIDE FLIGHT the first leaf rises as a swept broad trapezoid; a narrower second leaf extends above/behind it with a sharply clipped tip and a strong stepped rear contour. Make real overlap thickness and compact enclosed joint housings legible. No open framework or elongated hinge rods. Keep total height moderate, at most about the original Order tail's relative height.
Put the paired lateral mounting faces on the FIRST moving leaf, near its thick rear third, and one small upper pad on the SECOND leaf. The same pads remain rigidly attached to those same leaves in each state. This follows the useful idea of li_elite2, where CM/mine mounts belong to its middle moving spoiler and a turret mount to the upper moving section; do not depict actual equipment here.
In SIDE STOWED the TWO FULL-SIZE tail leaves make a modest pivot and short diagonal translation into greater overlap; the rear contour becomes shorter/less spread, and a substantial upright tail remains. Native reference motion is small: about 2 degrees and 9.74 degrees plus short slides, not a complete lay-down. Do not shrink, erase, telescope the whole leaf into nothing, or move the pads to the hull. Two-leaf side wings also fold as in the base, independently.
Locate the short tail root entirely behind the flush hatch between the motor housings; keep both motor tops empty of equipment pads and no crossbar. Preserve L64 body/engines/collar/wing contours. Label L66.
